paragraphs: The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea does not run its fostering service alone. It shares one service with Hammersmith and Fulham Council and Westminster City Council, so carers approved in the borough are part of a team that covers all three councils. Children in care from Kensington and Chelsea are looked after by that shared service and by independent agencies, including those shown above.

First enquiries go through Foster with West London, a recruitment hub that eight west London councils run together: Brent, Ealing, Hammersmith and Fulham, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, Kensington and Chelsea, and Westminster. You can get in touch online, by phone or on a video call, and when you are ready to apply you choose which council you want to foster for. The hub's privacy notice, updated in September 2024, sets out the checks that follow: a DBS check, personal and employer references, checks with former partners, and a medical, for you and any other adult in your home.

Neighbouring Hammersmith and Fulham, part of the same service, said in May 2025 that there are not enough foster carers in west London, with more than 700 needed across the area, and that the assessment usually takes about six months.

In March 2024 the borough shared the story of a foster carer from Earl's Court who had looked after 14 children over almost 20 years. She started after a friend suggested it, went to a meeting where she heard from other carers about the support on offer, and said a good network of the council, family and neighbours was what made it work.
Talk to Foster with West London and to two or three of the agencies above, and compare the training, out-of-hours support and payments each one offers.
